output.summary: A toxic autumn-blooming herbaceous perennial native to Great Britain and Ireland, autumn crocus produces flowers well before its leaves appear. It is lethally toxic because of colchicine, and its leaves have been mistaken by foragers for wild garlic.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are regarded as poisonous; corms have the highest toxin levels, and leaves have been mistaken by foragers for wild garlic.
